text:
**Caveat:** I had no code execution available in this session, so I counted by hand and cross-checked that every breakdown sums to the same totals (40 real accounts, 15 cancels). Please rerun it in pandas before relying on the numbers.

## Summary

The churn is real but smaller than the raw file suggests. The headline drops from 58.3% to 37.5% once trials and QA accounts are removed. Almost all of it is Pro at $69: 10 of 12 of those accounts cancelled, against 1 of 8 Pro accounts at $49 and 4 of 20 Basic accounts. Nine of the 15 real cancellations fall in August, and 3 more in September. Nothing in the file says why people left. A price change is a plausible hypothesis, but the data can't confirm it.

## Headline churn

| Set | Accounts | Cancelled | Churn |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw (all rows) | 60 | 35 | 58.3% |
| Excl. trials only | 45 | 20 | 44.4% |
| Excl. QA only | 55 | 30 | 54.5% |
| **Cleaned (no trials, no QA)** | **40** | **15** | **37.5%** |

These are cumulative churn rates (cancelled ÷ ever signed up), not monthly rates.

## Breakdowns (cleaned set)

**By plan and price**

| Segment | Accounts | Cancelled | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic $19 | 20 | 4 | 20.0% |
| Pro (all) | 20 | 11 | 55.0% |
| Pro $49 | 8 | 1 | 12.5% (small n) |
| Pro $69 | 12 | 10 | 83.3% |

**By signup cohort** (n=8 each, so rates are rough)

| Cohort | Accounts | Cancelled | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-03 | 8 | 3 | 37.5% |
| 2026-04 | 8 | 4 | 50.0% |
| 2026-05 | 8 | 2 | 25.0% |
| 2026-06 | 8 | 4 | 50.0% |
| 2026-07 | 8 | 2 | 25.0% (only 1–2 months of exposure) |

**By cancel month**

| Month | Cancels | Of which Pro $69 | Of which Basic | Share of cancels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| May | 1 | 0 (Pro $49) | 0 | 7% |
| Jun | 1 | 0 | 1 | 7% |
| Jul | 1 | 0 | 1 | 7% |
| Aug | 9 | 7 | 2 | 60% |
| Sep | 3 | 3 | 0 | 20% |

- **August:** 9 cancels out of 37 accounts still active at the start of the month, or about 24%.
- **September:** 3 out of 28, or about 11%.
- **Single-cancel months:** May, Jun and Jul have 1 cancel each, which is too few to read anything into.

## Main patterns

**Supported by the data**
- Churn is concentrated in Pro at $69. These accounts make up 30% of real accounts and 67% of real cancels.
- All 10 of those cancels happened in August or September.
- Pro at $49 has been stable since May. Its one cancel was in May, and the other 7 are still active.
- Basic churn is low and spread out across months and cohorts.
- Cohort differences (25–50%) are small-sample noise. The $69 accounts appear in every cohort from March to July, so this isn't a single bad cohort.

**Hypothesis only**
- A price increase from $49 to $69 may have triggered the August–September cancels. The Jul cohort having no $49 accounts fits a new price for new signups, and $69 accounts in earlier cohorts could be existing customers who were moved up.
- The file holds only the current price, so I can't see any price history.
- The timing also fits other August events, such as a product change, an outage, or an annual-renewal cluster.

**Data that would settle it**
- Price history per account, with the date each account moved to $69.
- Cancel reason codes or exit surveys.
- Renewal dates.
- Usage or engagement before cancelling.
- Whether the $69 accounts were migrated or newly signed up.

## Exclusions

- **15 trial accounts** (is_trial=yes, price $0; IDs 1009–1011, 1020–1022, 1031–1033, 1042–1044, 1053–1055).
  - All 15 cancelled the month after signup.
  - They aren't paying customers, so including them inflates churn.
  - The file has no row showing a trial converting, so trial conversion is unknown.
- **5 QA accounts** (@ourco.test, IDs 1056–1060).
  - All are Pro $69, signed up in Jul and cancelled in Aug.
  - They would add 5 cancels to August, to the $69 tier and to the Jul cohort, making all three look worse.
  - The .test domain and "qa" naming support your belief that they're internal, but the file can't prove it.

## Open questions

- Why did each account cancel? The file has no reason codes, so any cause is inference.
- Did pricing actually change, and did existing $49 accounts get moved to $69? Only the current price is recorded.
- Is September complete, and what happened in October? The file has no cancels after September, and today is Oct 6.
- Did any trials convert to paid? There are no linked rows.
- Are the groups big enough to rely on? Pro $49 (n=8), each cohort (n=8) and each single-cancel month are too small for confident rates.
